analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: the letter 'e'
key_insights: US stocks trade broadly higher on Tuesday 10/27, led by tech and consumer discretionary, as markets absorb solid macro data and a heavy earnings slate ahead of Wednesday's FOMC meeting.

Markets are leaning back into the AI infrastructure trade for a second day, with semis and most Mega Cap Tech higher. Concerns about peak AI investment and its returns remain, but investors are willing to buy into results from MSFT, GOOGL (Wednesday night) and AMZN (Thursday night).
Memory and semiconductor names reporting later this week: SK Hynix, Samsung, STX, SNDK, INTC, TER, NXPI, KLAC, ENTG, MPWR.

Staples: KO delivered a strong top-line beat on pricing power, emerging-market growth and margin expansion. SFD reported softer-than-expected results on volume and pricing declines across major meat segments. SFD trades up while KO trades lower.
Travel & Leisure: RCL, HLT and TNL results point to resilient travel demand. RCL shows stronger pricing momentum and booking visibility than the hotels.

Healthcare: CNC (insurer) and HCA (hospital) both reported strong results, but showed the impact of disruptions and changing enrollment in health insurance exchanges at both ends of the healthcare delivery chain.

FinTech: PYPL reported stronger-than-expected 3Q results on better transaction margins and lower opex. SOFI beat expectations and raised 2027 guidance on strong borrowing demand, high origination volumes and better NIM.

Data centers: JCI orders reaccelerated to +44% organically yoy (vs +27% in F3Q26), with backlog of $23.0bn up +43% yoy. XYL saw double-digit order growth in Applied Water on North American data center cooling demand. AMT beat EBITDA expectations but held guidance and flagged softer US organic growth.

Planes & Trucks: BA reported better-than-expected FCF and progress on revenue and margin drivers, but still faces higher supply chain costs and must stabilize its delivery timeline. UPS delivered a strong beat-and-raise on domestic shipping progress.
Paint & Copper: Higher raw material costs weighed on SHW's 3Q results despite strong operations. FCX reiterated 2026 Grasberg production guidance but lowered 2030 production guidance.

Info Services: SPGI reported stronger-than-expected revenue and margins and raised FY2026 guidance. Transaction revenue grew 1% (investment grade strong on hyperscaler deals and M&A, offset by softness in high yield, bank loans and structured finance), and non-transaction revenue grew 4%.

Macro data: the Conference Board's October Consumer Confidence came in well above expectations, in line with levels from the start of the year. September durable goods, ex-transportation durables and core capital goods shipments all rose.
GS raised its 3Q GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +3.4% qoq annualized after the capital goods data.

Chart of the Day: David Mericle expects the FOMC to skip a rate hike at tomorrow's meeting but likely deliver a second hike in December. Market pricing has removed one hike and now peaks at just over 4.5%.
GS baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are less hawkish than market pricing: GS is skeptical the FOMC will hike four times and expects cuts further down the road.

After the close Tuesday: HOOD, V, FFIV, ACGL, BXP, ESS, EXR, TER, CSGP, VTR, BKR, EQT, FE, OKE, PPG, WM, UHS and others report. Before the open Wednesday: APH, FLEX, TEL, VRT, FTV, GEV, LII, OTIS, GNRC, GRMN, MAS, ADP, BIIB, BSX, GEHC and others.

CNC and HCA reported strong results 10/27, with health insurance exchange enrollment disruption affecting both.
PYPL 3Q26 reported 10/27: stronger than expected on better transaction margins and lower opex.
SOFI 3Q26 reported 10/27: beat expectations and raised 2027 guidance on borrowing demand, origination volumes and NIM.
JCI F4Q26 reported 10/27: organic orders +44% yoy vs +27% organic in F3Q26, backlog $23.0bn +43% yoy.
XYL reported 10/27: double-digit order growth in Applied Water on North American data center cooling demand.
AMT 3Q26 reported 10/27: EBITDA beat versus expectations, guidance maintained, softer US organic growth.
BA 3Q26 reported 10/27: better-than-expected FCF, higher supply chain costs, delivery timeline still being stabilized.
UPS reported 10/27: beat-and-raise driven by domestic shipping operational progress.

tension_points.bull_case: Market pricing has removed one hike and peaks at just over 4.5%, which is less restrictive than previously priced.
tension_points.bear_case: GS expects the FOMC to skip October but hike again in December. Market pricing is still more hawkish than GS's baseline, which assumes only two hikes and cuts later.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hike at the 10/28 FOMC meeting or a hawkish path beyond two hikes would contradict the GS baseline.
